primary.how: 16291071 from the first-block-header opening read of the window starting there; 26022093 from the boundary-blocks read of the window ending there; every exit-0 collect bound the plan's finalized boundary at 26022093, which refuses unless the finalized tag stands at or above it; the tag's own number is not recorded by collect

second.how: 16291071 from the first-block-header opening read of the window starting there; 26022093 from the boundary-blocks read of the window ending there; every exit-0 collect bound the plan's finalized boundary at 26022093, which refuses unless the finalized tag stands at or above it; the tag's own number is not recorded by collect

release_byte_threshold.why: the study's 8,589,934,592-byte threshold was 128 components of 67,108,864 bytes, the release ceiling of the format #1888 replaced; the merged format allows 16,384 components, and the maintainer's 2026-09-24 ruling bounds each segment by the measured build and check memory alone

release_overhead.what: release bytes outside the logs and traces journals and the attribution parts, as a line through the two memory samples' shard counts: boundary headers, the opening journal, implementation code, registry, epoch table, reconciliation, plan and manifest

derivation.rule: shard width: the largest sampled span at or under the second transport's range cap and MAX_SHARD_WIDTH whose densest sampled logs stay within half of 20,000 and whose densest log and trace records stay within half of MAX_RESPONSE_NODES; shards_per_component: the largest count whose range, at the densest sampled span that covers it, keeps each class under three quarters of MAX_RAW_COMPONENT_BYTES and each part under MAX_PART_NODES; trace concurrency: the measured level with the most transactions per second; segments: as few as keep each estimated release times the memory ratio within three quarters of host memory, then as equal as that allows

attribution.from: mem-a's 23,243 attribution rows in its built parts

memory.ratio_rests_on: the largest peak resident set size of build and check over release bytes across the mem-a and mem-b sample releases, both collected on the primary and reconciled on the second transport; mem-a's build gives the maximum

collect_invocations.refusal: collection exceeded its total byte ceiling

collect_invocations.counts: not measured per class: the resumed tree's journal bytes are the component bytes this sample lists

reconcile_attempts.refusal: the interval is not completely collected, so there is nothing to reconcile
reconcile_attempts.why: it ran after the first collect invocation stopped at the 512 MiB per-invocation byte ceiling

reconcile_attempts.after: the second collect invocation completed the interval

node_events.event: the local node received SIGTERM and was down until the maintainer reloaded its jobs
the local node restarted and began its pipeline catch-up; primary timings after this are catch-up timings
primary collects began refusing with fast transport errors during catch-up; their JSON-RPC codes were not captured
the node's data volume disconnected temporarily and the node exited; runs from 11:25:30Z until the 11:27:00Z restart are node-unavailable
the volume was remounted and the node restarted without a configuration change

node_volume_disconnects.for_step_7: a collection must expect the primary to disappear for minutes and resume from its checkpoint
node_volume_disconnects.source: the operator, from the node launch wrapper's log

range.what: one eth_getLogs over 50,000 blocks answered; no range cap below MAX_SHARD_WIDTH

response_nodes_before_step_6.not_changed: trace_identity in scripts/usdc_interval.py still hashes each single trace frame under the canonical 200,000-node default when reconcile compares frames; only the six sites that write and read whole shard trace and log records moved to MAX_RESPONSE_NODES
response_nodes_before_step_6.refusal: staged logs response exceeds the 200000-node limit
response_nodes_before_step_6.what: before this step staged_results read a log response under the canonical 200,000-node default; after it, limit-p-5000-raised read the same 19,814 logs

sample_plans.subjects: every subject of examples/aave-v3-interval-v0/registry.json, in the order aave_registry.subject_entries gives
sample_plans.what: Each window's plan is this template over the window's interval, shard width and classes, with its provider class; its SHA-256 is recorded beside it and a test rebuilds it.

filter.evidence: every second-transport window's eth_getLogs named all 356 subjects and exited 0

trace_latency.excluded: windows phased latency-during-catch-up were taken while the node's pipeline was catching up and are not used
trace_latency.method: Each latency window is one collect with --concurrency 1 over 600 blocks in the dense region at the named --trace-concurrency; seconds are the collector's per-shard fetch times, whose traced transactions dominate them; windows are distinct so no answer is served from a warm cache.
trace_latency.node_state: taken after the node's head passed 26,046,733 and eth_blockNumber answered promptly; at the first sample the head was 26,048,161 with the pipeline finishing a 31-block tail (stage TransactionLookup, target 26,048,192), and at the last it was 26,048,459 and following the chain
trace_latency.refused: lat-steady-00-c1 stopped when one trace_transaction did not answer within the collector's 60-second per-request bound; it is recorded as refused and not averaged in

primary.class: local reth archive node, trace-enabled, loopback

second.class: hosted archive and trace provider, bearer-authenticated

what: Counts, bytes, timings, block hashes and command lines from bounded sample collections of the Aave V3 Ethereum main market over its ruled interval, on both transports, through the existing collect path. Staging trees and sample releases were discarded after measurement. Endpoints, headers and credentials are not recorded; providers are named by class.
